text: Lay awake doubting the whole idea again. Is a journal that remembers what you wrote actually worth building, and even if it is, can I execute it well enough on my own? I keep swinging between loving the idea and suspecting it only matters to me.

Read old entries on the bus and wondered whether I'm still the person who wrote them. The words are mine, but the worries and the certainty belong to someone slightly different. Maybe the self isn't one fixed thing, just a thread that memory keeps pulling through time.

Walked to the lake before breakfast with no plan at all. Two herons in the shallows, a warm croissant on the bench. Nothing was scheduled and that's exactly why it felt happy. The best moments keep turning up when the day is unplanned and ordinary, and this time I noticed it while it was happening.

It works! The app linked tonight's entry to one from months ago and I laughed out loud at my desk. I'm so excited to release this. Something I built start to finish will soon be in other people's hands, and I can't wait to share my work.

More doubt today. I'm one person with evenings while big companies have whole teams. I doubt the idea is strong enough, and I doubt I can execute it well alone. Every bug I fix makes me question both.

The ship of Theseus again: replace every plank and is it the same boat? Am I the same person I was a year ago when almost every belief has been swapped out? Perhaps identity survives because memory threads the old self to the new one.

Dinner at Maya's turned into a whole evening nobody planned. Someone burned the rice, we laughed until our cheeks hurt, and I walked home happy. It keeps happening: the happiest moments are the ordinary, unscheduled ones, and I'm getting better at noticing them in the moment.

Showed the demo to Sam and he said, 'oh, that's the thing.' I've been buzzing all afternoon. I'm so excited to release this and put my work in other people's hands. I can't wait to share something I built start to finish.

Reread my early project notes and doubted almost every idea in them. Maybe the reflections are too gentle, maybe remembering old entries is a gimmick. And even if the idea is good, can I really execute it alone? I can't tell if I'm refining the idea or losing faith in it.

Heraclitus said you can't step into the same river twice, because the river and you have both changed. Writing every day makes that feel literal. The person reading my old pages isn't quite the person who wrote them, yet memory lets me recognise myself in them.

Rain all afternoon, ginger tea by the window, an hour on the phone with Mum about nothing in particular. No plans, nothing to finish, and I felt completely happy. Again it was an ordinary, unplanned afternoon, and this time I noticed the happiness while it was happening.

Installer built and tested on a clean laptop. Release is almost here. Nervous, but mostly excited. I'm so excited to release it and share my work: something I made start to finish is about to be in other people's hands.

Doubt again, this time about execution. Letters, patterns, fonts, a writing dial: is the idea still clear, or am I hiding from shipping by adding features? I doubt the idea and I doubt my ability to execute it well alone, both at once.

If I forgot everything I'd written, would I still be me? Locke thought personal identity reaches exactly as far back as memory does. That's why this journal matters to me: it's a thread connecting who I was to who I'm becoming, even as the self keeps changing.

Saturday hike with the twins. We got lost twice and found a waterfall nobody had mentioned. Squashed sandwiches on a warm rock, legs wrecked, completely happy. The best days are still the ordinary, unplanned ones, and I'm learning to notice the happiness while I'm in it.

Tagged the release candidate and wrote the README tonight. For once the words came easily. I'm so excited to release this and put my work in other people's hands. Something I built start to finish is nearly ready to share.
A week before release and the doubt is loud again. I doubt the idea is good enough, and I doubt I've executed it well enough on my own. What if people open it once and never come back?

Am I the same person who wrote my first entry here, or someone new who just inherited the notes? Identity seems less like a fixed self and more like a thread, and remembering is how we keep pulling it through the changes.

Sunny morning, open window, pancakes on the balcony for no reason, a quick call to Maya just to say hi. Nothing planned and I felt so happy. The ordinary, unscheduled moments are where my happiness lives, and I noticed it right as it happened.

Tomorrow it goes public. Installer packed, release notes written, everything checked twice. Nervous, but mostly excited. Something I made is about to be in other people's hands. I can't wait to release it and share my work with the world.
